editorLatency.qualification: Small local samples with test activity. These measurements do not establish a speed change. An earlier sample taken during the full interpreter run was much slower and was repeated after that CPU-heavy run finished.

changes: Semantic array element metadata is independent of the materialized cell cache.
Runtime propagation reuses the analyzer binaryType rules; it does not probe operations or read lazy cells.
Bindings, copy, slices, transpose, reshape and preview copies carry available element information.
Previously typed bindings preserve their domain through empty/all-missing replacements without changing shared untyped sources.
Unresolved lazy element domains stay unresolved across reads and copies; return contracts still validate observed values.
Rank and full argument signatures use the same structural encoder. Existing direct array-element specialization granularity is retained.
Dense arithmetic and choose only borrow stored cells; they no longer probe unread operands and trigger callbacks/errors early.
reproductions: Source = array 1 2; Lazy = Source * 2 previously had a different argument key from Source and Lazy copy.
A stateful function could avoid its established result-type contract by copying a lazy input.
Calling twice on a 1024-cell lazy host array read its failing second cell before the result was consumed.

limitations: This does not introduce declaration syntax or an external-data validation API; these remain step 4 and issues 33/116.
Unknown element domains are conservative and do not become declared concrete types merely because their caches fill.
Record fields retain their existing eager structural validation.
Nested structure continues to be checked recursively at bindings and returns; array argument keys retain their existing direct-element granularity.
No runtime speed improvement is claimed.
